fields.claim_quote:
\noindent Given labeled graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$, a set $G_1 \sqcap\ G_2$ = \\$\{G \mid G \leq G_1, G_2, \quad
\forall G_* \leq G_1,G_2 \quad G_* \not\geq~G \}$ is called a set of \textbf{maximal common subgraphs} of graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$.
We also refer to $G_1 \sqcap G_2$ as to \textbf{intersection} of graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$, and to $\sqcap$ -- as to \textbf{similarity operator}
defined on graphs \cite{Kuz2013a}.
fields.explanation: The frozen source defines dominance by a full-domain vertex bijection, edge preservation, and label compatibility. Its displayed maximality condition forbids non-strict common supergraphs, including the candidate itself, so reflexivity excludes every common candidate. The versioned Lean certificate includes both injectivity and full-codomain surjectivity, retains the one-vertex witness, and also checks an edge-deletion control on a fixed two-vertex set. The strict-maximality repair is our separately labeled comparison predicate; no corrected wording is attributed to the source. This is a local definition-level counterexample, not a refutation of the paper's classification experiments.
fields.flaw: The displayed definition of $G_1 \sqcap G_2$ yields the set of maximal common subgraphs of two labeled graphs and therefore defines their graph intersection.
fields.problem: Title: Graphlet-based lazy associative graph classification
fields.witness: Let G1=G2=H be the one-vertex edgeless labeled graph with vertex label a. The identity is a bijection of the full vertex set and satisfies every edge and label condition, so H is common to H,H under the source dominance relation. The displayed universal condition allows G_*=H, but reflexivity gives H<=H, contradicting its required negation. H is maximal among common graphs: every such G_* already satisfies G_*<=H and therefore cannot be strictly above H. The versioned selected Lean theorem proves these facts using the full-domain bijective relation.

scope_metadata.formal_relation: A bijection between the full vertex types, preserving edges and vertex/edge label compatibility. The same relation defines commonness, strict containment and maximality.
scope_metadata.source_version_scope: The exact supplied frozen source at lines128–133 and170–173; the record identifier alone does not establish a public version attribution.
scope_metadata.target_scope: The literal non-strict exclusion in the maximal-common-subgraph definition, using the source full-domain bijective relation.
